'''''Oxalis dillenii''''', the '''southern wood-sorrel''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Slender Yellow Woodsorrel, Southern Yellow Wood-sorrel, Dillen's Oxalis - Oxalis dillenii |url=https://uswildflowers.com/detail.php?SName=Oxalis%20dillenii |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=uswildflowers.com}}</ref> '''slender yellow woodsorrel''', or '''Dillen's oxalis''',<ref>{{ITIS|id=29074|taxon=''Oxalis dillenii''|access-date=6 May 2022}}</ref> is a species in the [[Oxalidaceae|woodsorrel family]]. Like other ''Oxalis'' species, the leaves of this plant resemble [[clover]] leaves, with three leaflets. ''Oxalis dillenii'' can be confused with other small yellow flowered species in North America, such as ''[[Oxalis stricta]]''  and ''Oxalis florida''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Digital Atlas of the Virginia Flora {{!}} Oxalis dillenii Jacquin |url=https://www.vaplantatlas.org/index.php?do=plant&plant=3099&search=Search |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=www.vaplantatlas.org}}</ref> The flowers have five yellow petals that are {{cvt|4|to|10|mm|in}} in length. The leaflets are {{cvt|1|to|2|cm|in}} wide with pointed hairs. The fruits are rather brown and are {{cvt|1.5|to|2.5|cm|in}}. It is often considered a [[weed]], and can be found worldwide, but likely originated in [[North America]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Gleason & Cronquist|title=Manual of Vascular Plants of Northeastern United States and Adjacent Canada|date=1991|publisher=The New York Botanical Garden|edition=2nd}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Oxalis dillenii'' was given its scientific name by [[Nikolaus Joseph von Jacquin]] in 1794. It is part of the genus ''[[Oxalis]]'' within the family [[Oxalidaceae]] and it has {{table row counter|id=Synonyms}} [[Synonym (botany)|synonyms]].<ref name="POWO">{{cite POWO |id= |title=''Oxalis dillenii'' Jacq. |access-date=14 December 2025}}</ref>

==Ecology==

''Oxalis dillenii'' is insect pollinated and is recorded to have been visited in northern Florida by ''[[Augochloropsis metallica]]'', ''[[Bombus impatiens]]'', ''[[Ceratina]]'', ''Lasioglossum creberrimum'', ''[[Lasioglossum pectorale]]'', ''Lasioglossum tegulare/puteulanum'', ''[[Lasioglossum vierecki]]'',and ''Lasioglossum weemsi/leviense''. <ref>Ulyshen, M. D., K. Robertson, S. Horn, and C. Dixon. 2024. Characterization of the bee community and pollination network in a southeastern U.S. pine savanna. Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution 12:1403602.</ref>
